error.protocol_version: The IPC protocol version is unsupported. Update the CLI and agent together.

error.timeout: The operation timed out. Check the adapter and enable DDC/CI in the monitor menu.

help.generic: This setting is saved for your user account and used by the background agent. Hover or click the question mark to keep this explanation open.
help.rawInput: Most monitors use MCCS values: DisplayPort 1 = 15 (0x0F), DisplayPort 2 = 16 (0x10), HDMI 1 = 17 (0x11), HDMI 2 = 18 (0x12). Your monitor may use a different value. Enter decimal 1–255 or hex 0x01–0xFF. Adding a custom input does not run a monitor command.
help.inputAlias: Give this input a name such as “MacBook” or “Gaming PC”. The tile keeps its port type (for example HDMI 2) and displays your name alongside it. The name also appears in rules and the setup wizard. Renaming does not switch the monitor.
help.ruleName: A short name for this automation, such as “Switch to MacBook”. It only changes the label shown in the app and CLI.
help.profileName: A profile groups your switching rules. One profile is active at a time. Creating another profile keeps it inactive until you activate it. The wizard creates and activates a default profile for you.
help.trigger: Connect runs when the selected USB group arrives on this computer. Disconnect runs when it leaves. These are USB presence events, not proof that the monitor switched. The wizard creates one rule for each direction.
help.combination: All: every selected device must reach the target state. Any: one selected device is enough. At least N: the threshold you choose must reach that state. Use All for a keyboard and mouse that move together; use At least N when an optional device sometimes stays connected.
help.minimum: For At least N, enter a whole number from 1 to the number of selected devices. For example, 2 of 3 tolerates one device remaining on this host. Logical physical devices are counted once, not once for each HID interface.
help.devices: Choose the USB devices that actually move with the KVM. Use the setup wizard to see disconnect and reconnect timing. Receivers and hubs may represent several peripherals; avoid selecting both duplicate interfaces of the same physical receiver.
help.targetMonitor: Choose the external monitor that should receive this rule’s input command. Selection is by saved hardware identity, not by screen position. Built-in MacBook displays are excluded because they have no external KVM input to switch.
help.targetInput: Choose a standard or custom input tile. You may choose yellow unverified inputs immediately; tests are optional. A green dot means that value has been read back from the monitor. Custom names are edited on the Monitors screen.
help.debounce: How long the target USB state must remain stable before the rule runs. Default 0 ms reacts immediately to a fresh transition. If your KVM briefly disconnects and reconnects several times, try 100–400 ms to ignore those short glitches. Allowed: 0–60000 ms.
help.cooldown: Minimum time between executions of this same rule. Default 500 ms; 0 disables this limit. A new USB transition is still required, so a stable disconnected device does not repeatedly run the rule. Increase this if a noisy KVM causes repeated switches. Allowed: 0–120000 ms.
help.rearm: How long the USB group must stay in the opposite state before the rule can trigger again. Example: a disconnect rule rearms after devices have been connected for this period. Default 500 ms prevents a tiny bounce from counting as a new switch. Allowed: 0–60000 ms.
help.coincidence: Optional maximum spread between USB device events in one group. Example: a keyboard disappears now and a mouse 800 ms later; a 1000 ms window accepts the group. A 300 ms window rejects that slow group. 0 disables this extra timing check. This is separate from debounce, which waits after the group reaches its target state. Allowed: 0–120000 ms.
help.command: Run a local shell command on this USB direction, using the same group and timing as the rule. Commands are optional and work with the GUI closed. Automatic commands obey profile/rule enable and dry run. Use absolute executable paths when the login agent has a different PATH than your terminal.
help.commandShell: System uses PowerShell on Windows, zsh on macOS and sh on Linux. Bash and PowerShell can be selected explicitly if installed. Command Prompt is Windows-only. No terminal window or administrator elevation is opened.
help.commandTimeout: Maximum duration of one custom command, including shell startup. Default 10000 ms. On timeout the helper and its process tree are terminated; exit/output details appear in Event log. Allowed: 100–300000 ms. This is separate from the monitor DDC timeout.
help.commandDirectory: Folder in which the shell starts. Empty means your user home. Relative paths are resolved from home; the folder must exist. This changes where relative file names in your command point.
help.commandsEnabled: Enables the saved shell commands for this rule’s USB group. At least one command is required. Profile and rule enable states still apply. A manual test explicitly runs the saved command even when automatic execution is disabled.
help.activeProfile: Exactly one profile is active in the interface. Activating a profile stops the other profiles from triggering. Inside it, each rule can be enabled or disabled separately. Existing configurations with multiple active profiles use the first active profile when loaded.
help.theme: System follows the operating system’s light or dark appearance and is the default for a fresh installation. Light and Dark override it for this app only. Existing saved choices are kept.
help.uiMode: Window-only shows the desktop window. Both adds a tray/menu-bar icon. Tray-only and menu-bar-only keep quick controls without a normal taskbar window. Headless hides the interface; use the standalone agent for a process with no GUI at all.
help.closeAction: Hide keeps Elarydil KVM in the menu bar and switching keeps working. Quit GUI closes the app; the agent then stops too, unless “Keep agent running when the app quits” is on.
help.language: Application text currently ships in English. The shared text catalog is used by the desktop interface, CLI help and errors.
help.agentLogin: Starts only the background agent at sign-in, without the app or menu-bar icon. Available when the standalone agent is enabled. The operating system may ask for approval.
help.guiLogin: Opens Elarydil KVM when you sign in. Automatic switching runs while the app is open or in the menu bar.
help.globalCooldown:
Safety gap between two input switches on the same monitor, across all rules and manual switching. It stops two rules from fighting and flipping the monitor back and forth.

Keep it short: if it is 5000 ms and you press the KVM switch again within 5 seconds, the return switch is ignored and the monitor stays on the wrong input. 100 ms (the default) is enough against flapping. 0 disables it. Reversible 15-second tests are not affected.
help.startupGrace: When the agent starts (at login, after opening the app or after a rule change), USB devices are still being listed and some appear late. During this period the agent only records which devices are present, so a device that was already missing is not mistaken for a fresh disconnect that would switch your monitor. It does not delay normal KVM switches. Default 3000 ms.
help.resumeGrace: After sleep/wake or a USB watcher restart, devices reconnect in bursts as the system wakes up. During this period the agent rebuilds its picture of connected devices instead of treating those reconnects as a KVM switch. It does not delay normal KVM switches. Default 4000 ms.
help.dryRun: When enabled, matching events are logged but monitor writes and automatic custom commands do not execute. It is off by default. Use it to inspect a new rule without changing hardware. Explicit manual input/command tests still execute after confirmation.
help.setting.startupDelayMs: Additional wait when the agent starts, useful when a dock or USB hub takes several seconds to appear after login. It is added to startup grace once, not to every switch. Allowed: 0–120000 ms.
help.setting.defaultDebounceMs: Initial debounce used when creating rules through the CLI. Default 0 ms. Each existing rule keeps its own value; changing this does not rewrite old rules. Try a small delay only if USB presence bounces. Allowed: 0–60000 ms.
help.setting.commandTimeoutMs: Maximum time for one monitor DDC operation, not a custom shell command. Default 2000 ms. Slow adapters may need more; a high value can make a failed read or write take longer to report. Live reads never overlap and back off after failures. Allowed: 100–30000 ms.
help.diagnosticReport: Download a local diagnostic report with command text, command output, device serials and local paths redacted. It helps investigate problems without exporting the full private configuration. No report is uploaded automatically.
help.configuration: Export every setting, hardware selector, profile and custom shell command. This is a full private backup rather than a redacted report. Import it through the CLI after reviewing host-specific monitor and USB identities.
help.daemon: The agent watches USB devices, runs your rules, returns tested inputs and runs custom commands. Pause stops automatic rules; resume starts from a fresh baseline. Restart replaces the agent process; Stop ends it.

ui.agentStandalone: Keep agent running when the app quits
ui.agentStandaloneDetail: For advanced setups. When off, switching works while Elarydil KVM is open or in the menu bar and stops when you quit it.
help.agentStandalone:
The agent is the small background process that watches USB devices and switches monitor inputs; the window and menu-bar icon only configure it.

Off (default): the agent starts and stops together with Elarydil KVM.
On: the agent keeps working after you quit the app, invisible except in Activity Monitor (elarydil-kvm-agent).

Stop it from Terminal:
"/Applications/Elarydil KVM.app/Contents/Resources/bin/elarydil-kvm" agent stop
Check it:
"/Applications/Elarydil KVM.app/Contents/Resources/bin/elarydil-kvm" agent status
Remove its login start:
"/Applications/Elarydil KVM.app/Contents/Resources/bin/elarydil-kvm" startup disable --component agent
